_rule: This is PACK DATA on the EDU engine. Adding a subject is adding a FILE, never editing the engine. The engine owns sequencing, mastery, and the honesty rules; this file only names the subject matter, the FUNDING, and the DATES.
_source: All funding figures verified 2026-10-26 from AtoZ screenshots (read directly) + provider pages. Funding amounts are Jordan's own account values, not estimates.
_revision: REVISED 2026-10-27 — Jordan set the endgame: 'I want the focus to be on cloud engineering because of not only the income potential, but being able to work remote.' Consequence: SANS CyberLaunch is OUT (its entry seat is SOC Tier-1 triage, which the AI-substitutability measurement ranked the highest-confidence avoid, and its budget year competes with nothing useful). The minor moves from GIAC to CYFRIN UPDRAFT (Solidity + smart-contract security) — free, no budget impact, and it feeds the recorded 'minor in Solidity and blockchain security for Cypherin' intent.
_honesty_rules: NEVER print progress as a fact about the learner. This is a plan, not certification.
No observed work on a milestone means UNMEASURED — never a fabricated 0%.
COVERAGE IS NOT PROFICIENCY: knowing the plan is not passing an exam. Only a certificate number closes one.
An unattempted milestone is NOT a miss — exclude it from any ratio rather than counting it against him.
DEADLINES ARE HARD DATES, not nudges. The per-year voucher cap is a real gate.
A began-course is NOT a credential. A cert closes when a Pearson VUE result exists.
A FREE COURSE HAS NO DEADLINE — never let Cyfrin's open access displace a voucher-windowed AWS exam. Order matters.

target.lane_reason: Not only income (entry $110k-$130,802 vs $52-72k for cyber entry), but REMOTE viability — which is the hard requirement he named. Data-center ops was evaluated and rejected for exactly this: it is on-site by definition.

target.strategy: COMPOUND, not escape. Stay employed; harvest the benefits; build years while credentialed.
target.why_this_works: The measured FDE gate was '2-6+ years, mostly 5+'. This plan BUILDS those years while employed rather than waiting for them. By 2028 the candidate is ~3 years at Amazon + cloud certs + a rare cloud/security blend + a live operating portfolio.
target.explicitly_not: NOT a 6-month exit plan. That pressure was removed by Jordan's own decision on 2026-10-26.

Web3 — the x402 rail, ERC-8004 identity, Treasury work

_pitfalls._what: Money and time traps previous students hit. Each one is a RULE the engine can surface in a lesson when the learner reaches the milestone it protects.
_pitfalls._source: r/AWSCertifications (2022-2026) including the engineer who created the Skill Builder exam-prep courses, plus official AWS training pricing (2026-10-28).
_pitfalls._limit: Forum evidence, not a controlled study. The population that posts skews toward people who struggled. Treat these as warnings that cost little to obey — not as measured failure rates.
_pitfalls._standing_rule: CHECK THE FREE DOOR FIRST. Amazon already funds this: Skill Builder free to employees, one 100% exam voucher per year via AtoZ, and Career Choice $5,250 for 2027. Anyone paying before confirming those three is paying for something already owned.

pitfalls.trap: Buying a video course when the free tier covers the concepts
pitfalls.what_happens: Skill Builder's free tier is 600+ courses. The paid tier's real addition is the OFFICIAL PRACTICE EXAM, not better teaching.
pitfalls.rule: Never buy a course to LEARN. Buy the readiness test only when the exam date is set.

pitfalls.what_happens: $29/month running for a 3-month study plan = $87 for what ONE month buys.
pitfalls.rule: Buy Skill Builder Individual for the month you SIT the exam. Cancel after. One month, not three.

pitfalls.trap: Buying more than one practice-exam bank
pitfalls.what_happens: People stack Tutorials Dojo AND WhizLabs AND the instructor's exams. They test the same patterns; the second bank teaches nothing new.
pitfalls.rule: ONE outside bank. Practise the question SHAPES, not new answers.

pitfalls.trap: Treating a course as evidence of readiness
pitfalls.what_happens: The exam-prep course is a READINESS CHECK by design — the engineer who built it says so: 'designed to help you identify skills gaps and determine your readiness.' Using it as the teacher is using a thermometer as a textbook.
pitfalls.rule: Readiness is a PRACTICE-EXAM SCORE, never hours watched. No score = UNMEASURED, not ready.
pitfalls.cost_if_ignored: a retake — $150, or a wasted annual voucher (2027 benefit burns)

pitfalls.trap: Paying for what Amazon already funds
pitfalls.what_happens: Skill Builder is free to employees, the 100% voucher comes from AtoZ, and Career Choice has $5,250 unspent. Buying first pays twice for one thing.
pitfalls.rule: AtoZ check BEFORE any card is entered. Three questions: is Skill Builder active, is the voucher claimed, what is Career Choice allocated to.

pitfalls.what_happens: Postings in a 98-posting sample name Kubernetes and GPU serving. NOT ONE asked for a certificate. The cert closes a benefit that would otherwise be wasted; it does not close the hiring gap.
pitfalls.rule: The cert is a funded credential, never the door to the job. APPLY IN PARALLEL — do not wait for it.
pitfalls.cost_if_ignored: months of opportunity cost, not dollars

pitfalls.trap: Front-loading the certs past the hard date
pitfalls.what_happens: The voucher is one per YEAR and the SANS cohort starts 2027-02-15 at 16-20 hrs/week. If the AWS certs are not landed before then, they wait a full year.
pitfalls.rule: The AWS window closes 2027-02-15. Land them EARLY in the window, not at the end of it.
